A preference is a starting point, but a usable finding names what happened and how it affected the task. The explanation is tentative. Maybe the label caused the pause, or maybe the task setup was unclear. Change one relevant thing and retest. Record strengths with the same care: a tester finding the target without help is evidence of a successful interaction. If no issue appeared, say that instead of inventing one.

title: Usage Logs and Observation
text: Did it complete, and how long did it take?
Did the message help the user recover?

Which evidence would help explain a slow task in your tool?
notes:
Telemetry can record operation counts, durations and reasons for blocked actions. Observation can reveal hesitation, workarounds and misunderstanding. Combine them when useful, but do not equate a click count or successful call with a good experience. Collect only fields needed for the question and avoid copying project paths or user content unnecessarily. For this class, a short observation record is enough; we are not adding a telemetry implementation requirement.

title: Peer Review Roles
text: Rotate roles after each seven-minute round.
Each tool gets one test with two peers.
notes:
Form groups of three and choose A, B and C. Each round focuses on one tool. The owner explains the goal and prepared input, then watches. The tester tries the task and says what they expect. The observer records the visible evidence and any coaching. Rotate so each person owns, tests and observes once. This is one observed attempt per tool, not three independent tests of every tool. If a group has an extra member, they can observe without inflating the number of distinct attempts.

Use the final minute to specify the retest and reset, not to start another feature. The timer will stop at the end of the round; choose the next round deliberately. A proposed visual change remains a hypothesis until you test it. Record which mode you used, what was observed and what remains untested.
